question:
A 25-year-old female presents for a routine wellness visit. Her medical history reveals three episodes of
gonorrhea and chlamydia treatment within the last six months. She currently uses oral contraceptive
pills successfully for the past year. Her social history includes cigarette smoking and regular alcohol
consumption, though she practices safety by wearing a helmet while cycling. Her physical examination
and vital signs are normal. She seeks advice about contraception options and sexual health. Given her
clinical presentation and history, what would be the most suitable recommendation? Answer Choices:
(A) Additional use of condoms (B) Recommending abstinence until monogamous relationship (C) Dual
therapy with oral contraceptives and injectable contraception (D) Switching to contraceptive patch (E)
Continuing current oral contraceptive regimen (F) Switching to intrauterine device (G) Switching to
injectable contraception (H) Regular STI screening only (I) Switching to vaginal ring (J) Tubal ligation
 A. Continuing current oral contraceptive regimen
B. Switching to intrauterine device
C. Recommending abstinence until monogamous relationship
D. Additional use of condoms
E. Dual therapy with oral contraceptives and injectable contraception

F. Regular STI screening only
G. Switching to vaginal ring
H. Tubal ligation
I. Switching to contraceptive patch
J. Switching to injectable contraception
